278	class FleetSimulator:
279	    def __init__(self, grid: GridMap, robots: list[Robot], tasks: list[Task]) -> None:
280	        self.grid = grid
281	        # The map as built before any runtime edit; map-change history is
282	        # replayed against this baseline.
283	        self.base_grid = grid
284	        self.robots = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
285	        self.tasks = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
286	        self.tick = 0
287	        self.replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
288	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
289	        self._map_sequence = 0
290	        self.paused_tasks: set[str] = set()
291	        # Consecutive per-robot waits caused purely by other robots:
292	        # robot_id -> {"blocked_by": [robot_id, ...], "ticks": int}.
293	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
294	        positions = [robot.position for robot in robots]
295	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
296	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
297	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):
298	            raise ValueError("robot starts outside traversable map space")
299	        self._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
300	        # Accepted routes share one internal shape regardless of how the caller
301	        # spelled them: a mutable list of tuple cells. The normalized copies are
302	        # committed only after every robot passed validation, so a rejection
303	        # (even one buried in a later robot's route) never touches the caller's
304	        # objects. See :meth:`_normalize_initial_routes`.
305	        normalized_routes = self._normalize_initial_routes(grid, robots)
306	        for robot, route in zip(robots, normalized_routes):
307	            robot.route = route
308	
309	    @staticmethod
310	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
311	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
312	
313	        The very same mutual-ownership requirement backs direct construction
314	        and checkpoint loading, so it lives in exactly one place. The binding
315	        only governs work still in progress:
316	
317	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
318	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
319	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
320	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
321	          collected additionally must have an owner.
322	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
323	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
324	
325	        Completed tasks only keep *historical* ownership: their recorded
326	        ``assigned_robot`` is not required to be idle or to name them back, so
327	        a robot that already finished one task may be idle or busy with a new
328	        one. Unassigned, not-yet-collected tasks simply wait -- even when no
329	        robot can reach them -- and are not an ownership error. Nothing here
330	        rewrites a binding or drops a task; an inconsistent input is rejected
331	        as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the conflicting robot or
332	        task, leaving the caller's objects untouched.
333	        """
334	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
335	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
336	        for robot in robots:
337	            if robot.task_id is None:
338	                continue
339	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
340	            if task is None:
341	                raise ValueError(
342	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
343	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
344	                )
345	            if task.completed:
346	                raise ValueError(
347	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
348	                    "that is already completed"
349	                )
350	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
351	                raise ValueError(
352	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
353	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
354	                )
355	        for task in tasks:
356	            # Completed tasks retain historical ownership; their robots are
357	            # free to take new work, so the mutual binding only holds while a
358	            # task is still in progress.
359	            if task.completed:
360	                continue
361	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
362	                raise ValueError(
363	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
364	                )
365	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
366	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
367	                if owner is None:
368	                    raise ValueError(
369	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
370	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
371	                    )
372	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
373	                    raise ValueError(
374	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
375	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
376	                    )
377	
378	    @staticmethod
379	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
380	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
381	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
382	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
383	
384	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound: a route carries no current
385	        cell, so a non-empty route must begin with an orthogonal neighbour of
386	        the robot's position and every later waypoint must be one orthogonal
387	        step from the previous one. Diagonal moves, multi-cell jumps, two
388	        identical consecutive waypoints and a first waypoint equal to the
389	        current cell are all rejected, and every waypoint must lie inside the
390	        map and outside its obstacles. The outer route may be a list or tuple
391	        and each waypoint may itself be a list or tuple of two plain integers
392	        -- booleans are not integers here, and wrong lengths or element types
393	        raise :class:`ValueError` instead of leaking unpacking or hashing
394	        failures. The forms may be mixed freely; only the coordinate order
395	        matters, not the container types.
396	
397	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
398	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
399	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
400	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
401	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
402	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
403	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
404	
405	        The check is read-only -- normalization happens on fresh lists, and
406	        the caller commits them itself only once every robot has passed, so a
407	        rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a later robot or at
408	        the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders or otherwise
409	        modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. Checkpoint loading
410	        keeps its own, stricter validation that also covers the task
411	        pickup/dropoff rules.
412	        """
413	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
414	        for robot in robots:
415	            route = robot.route
416	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
417	                raise ValueError(
418	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
419	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
420	                )
421	            waypoints: list[Position] = []
422	            previous = robot.position
423	            for index, cell in enumerate(route):
424	                waypoint = _as_cell(
425	                    cell, f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
426	                )
427	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
428	                    raise ValueError(
429	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
430	                        f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
431	                    )
432	                if index == 0 and waypoint == previous:
433	                    raise ValueError(
434	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 "
435	                        f"{list(waypoint)} is the robot's current cell; the "
436	                        "remaining route must start with the next cell"
437	                    )
438	                if waypoint == previous:
439	                    raise ValueError(
440	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route repeats cell "
441	                        f"{list(waypoint)} at consecutive waypoints "
442	                        f"{index - 1} and {index}"
443	                    )
444	                if (
445	                    abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
446	                    + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
447	                    != 1
448	                ):
449	                    if index == 0:
450	                        segment = (
451	                            f"from its current position {list(previous)} to "
452	                            f"route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
453	                        )
454	                    else:
455	                        segment = (
456	                            f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} "
457	                            f"to waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
458	                        )
459	                    raise ValueError(
460	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently "
461	                        f"{segment}: every step must move one orthogonal cell"
462	                    )
463	                waypoints.append(waypoint)
464	                previous = waypoint
465	            normalized.append(waypoints)
466	        return normalized

468	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
469	    # Dynamic map edits
470	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
471	
472	    def modify_obstacles(
473	        self,
474	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
475	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
476	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
477	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
478	
479	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
480	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
481	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
482	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
483	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
484	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
485	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
486	
487	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
488	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
489	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
490	        distance is accumulated.
491	        """
492	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
493	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
494	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
495	        if conflict:
496	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
497	            raise ValueError(
498	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
499	            )
500	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
501	        for cell in add_cells:
502	            if cell in occupied:
503	                raise ValueError(
504	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
505	                )
506	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
507	
508	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
509	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
510	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
511	        seen: set[Position] = set()
512	        ordered: list[Position] = []
513	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
514	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
515	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
516	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
517	            if position in seen:
518	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
519	                continue
520	            seen.add(position)
521	            ordered.append(position)
522	        return ordered
523	
524	    def _apply_map_change(
525	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
526	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
527	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
528	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
529	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
530	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
531	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
532	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
533	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
534	
535	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
536	        # known to change the map.
537	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
538	        self._map_sequence += 1
539	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
540	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
541	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
542	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
543	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
544	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
545	
546	    def _map_change_record(
547	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
548	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
549	        return {
550	            "type": "map_change",
551	            "tick": self.tick,
552	            "sequence": sequence,
553	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
554	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
555	        }
556	
557	    def _plan_route(
558	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
559	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
560	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
561	
562	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
563	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
564	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
565	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
566	        """
567	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
568	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
569	
570	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
571	        for task in self.tasks.values():
572	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
573	                continue
574	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
575	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
576	                continue
577	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
578	            if route is None:
579	                robot.route = []
580	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
581	            else:
582	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
583	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
584	                robot.route = route
585	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
586	
587	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
588	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
589	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
590	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
591	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
592	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
593	                continue
594	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
595	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
596	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
597	                continue
598	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
599	            if route is None:
600	                robot.route = []
601	                continue
602	            robot.route = route
603	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
604	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
605	
606	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
607	    # Traffic conflicts and yielding
608	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
609	
610	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
611	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
612	        cells: set[Position] = set()
613	        for robot in self.robots.values():
614	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
615	                cells.update(robot.route)
616	        return cells
617	
618	    def _safe_side_cells(
619	        self,
620	        robot: Robot,
621	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
622	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
623	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
624	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
625	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
626	
627	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
628	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
629	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
630	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
631	
632	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
633	          skips anything else),
634	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
635	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
636	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
637	          route is excluded), and
638	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
639	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
640	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
641	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
642	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
643	
644	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
645	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
646	        """
647	        blocked = set(forbidden)
648	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
649	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
650	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
651	                continue
652	            yield cell
653	
654	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
655	        self,
656	        blocker: Robot,
657	        requester: Robot,
658	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
659	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
660	    ) -> Position | None:
661	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
662	
663	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
664	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
665	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
666	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
667	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
668	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
669	        """
670	        return next(
671	            self._safe_side_cells(
672	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
673	            ),
674	            None,
675	        )
676	
677	    def _self_sidestep(
678	        self,
679	        robot: Robot,
680	        task: Task | None,
681	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
682	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
683	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
684	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
685	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
686	
687	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
688	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
689	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
690	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
691	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
692	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
693	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
694	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
695	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
696	        """
697	        if task is None or task.completed:
698	            return None
699	        destination = robot.route[0]
700	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
701	        if blocker_id is None:
702	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
703	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
704	        best_length = 0
705	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
706	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
707	        # that order as the tie break.
708	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
709	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
710	            if route is None:
711	                continue
712	            if (
713	                blocker_id is not None
714	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
715	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
716	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
717	                )
718	            ):
719	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
720	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
721	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
722	                continue
723	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
724	                best = (cell, route)
725	                best_length = len(route)
726	        return best
727	
728	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
729	        self,
730	        robot: Robot,
731	        side: Position,
732	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
733	        blocker_id: str,
734	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
735	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
736	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
737	    ) -> bool:
738	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
739	
740	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
741	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
742	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
743	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
744	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
745	        never rejected here.
746	        """
747	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
748	            return False
749	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
750	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
751	            return False
752	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
753	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
754	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
755	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
756	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
757	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
758	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
759	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
760	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
761	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
762	        return not self._can_vacate(
763	            blocker,
764	            robot,
765	            hyp_occupied,
766	            reserved,
767	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
768	            blocked_path,
769	        )
770	
771	    def _can_vacate(
772	        self,
773	        blocker: Robot,
774	        requester: Robot,
775	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
776	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
777	        checking: frozenset[str],
778	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
779	    ) -> bool:
780	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
781	
782	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
783	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
784	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
785	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
786	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
787	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
788	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave check
789	        is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
790	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
791	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
792	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
793	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
794	        the blocker's own route does).
795	        """
796	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
797	            return False
798	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
799	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
800	            return False
801	        if not blocker.route:
802	            if task is not None:
803	                # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
804	                # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
805	                return False
806	            # A parked robot (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
807	            # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
808	            # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
809	            # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
810	            # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
811	            # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
812	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
813	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
814	        ahead = blocker.route[0]
815	        if (
816	            self.grid.traversable(ahead)
817	            and ahead not in occupied
818	            and ahead not in reserved
819	        ):
820	            return True
821	        occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
822	        if (
823	            occupant_id is not None
824	            and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
825	            and occupant_id not in checking
826	        ):
827	            # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
828	            # vacates its cell this same tick.
829	            if self._can_vacate(
830	                self.robots[occupant_id],
831	                requester,
832	                occupied,
833	                reserved,
834	                checking | {blocker.robot_id},
835	                blocked_path,
836	            ):
837	                return True
838	        if task is None:
839	            # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
840	            # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
841	            # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
842	            return False
843	        # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
844	        # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
845	        # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
846	        for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
847	            blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
848	        ):
849	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
850	                return True
851	        return False
852	
853	    def _update_traffic_waits(
854	        self,
855	        waited: dict[str, str],
856	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
857	    ) -> None:
858	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
859	
860	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
861	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
862	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
863	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
864	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
865	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
866	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
867	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
868	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
869	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
870	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
871	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
872	        """
873	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
874	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
875	        for robot_id in waited:
876	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
877	                continue
878	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
879	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
880	                continue
881	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
882	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
883	                continue

886	                continue

888	            if entry is None:
889	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}

897	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
898	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
899	
900	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
901	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
902	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
903	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
904	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
905	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
906	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
907	        """
908	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
909	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
910	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
911	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
912	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
913	                continue
914	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
915	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]

917	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:

919	            {
920	                "robot_id": robot_id,
921	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
922	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
923	            }
924	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
925	        ]

931	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
932	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest available robot using stable tie breaks.
933	
934	        Only a robot with no bound task *and* no remaining route is available:
935	        a taskless robot still driving a preset route keeps that route and is
936	        never selected, even when it is the closest to the pickup -- being
937	        temporarily blocked by traffic does not count as having finished the
938	        route either. Skipping such a robot never touches its position,
939	        mileage, cargo state or remaining waypoints, and never makes other
940	        tasks wait: the next available robot is chosen by the usual shortest
941	        feasible route length with the robot id string as tie break.
942	        """
943	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
944	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
945	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
946	            for robot in self.robots.values():
947	                if not robot.idle or robot.route:
948	                    continue
949	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
950	                if route is None:
951	                    continue
952	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
953	            if not choices:
954	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
955	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
956	                continue
957	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
958	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
959	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
960	            robot.route = route
961	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
962	
963	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
964	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
965	        for robot in self.robots.values():
966	            if robot.task_id is None:
967	                continue
968	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
969	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
970	                task.picked_up = True
971	
972	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
973	        self._confirm_pickups()
974	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
975	        self.assign_tasks()
976	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
977	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
978	        self._confirm_pickups()
979	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
980	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
981	        moved: list[str] = []
982	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
983	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
984	
985	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
986	            del occupied[robot.position]
987	            robot.position = destination
988	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
989	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
990	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
991	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
992	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
993	
994	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
995	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
996	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
997	                continue
998	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
999	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1000	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
1001	                continue
1002	            if not robot.route:
1003	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1004	                continue
1005	            destination = robot.route[0]
1006	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
1007	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
1008	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
1009	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
1010	                    if route is None:
1011	                        robot.route = []
1012	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
1013	                    else:
1014	                        robot.route = route
1015	                continue
1016	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
1017	            if blocker_id is None:
1018	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
1019	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
1020	                relocate(robot, destination)
1021	                robot.route.pop(0)
1022	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1023	                continue
1024	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
1025	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
1026	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
1027	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
1028	                if blocker.task_id is None and not blocker.route:
1029	                    # Truly parked blocker: no bound task and no remaining
1030	                    # route. Ask it to yield onto a free side cell, then take
1031	                    # over the cell it vacated. A taskless robot that still has
1032	                    # a remaining route is not parked: it drives that route
1033	                    # cell by cell like any other moving robot and is never
1034	                    # pushed off it for a requester.
1035	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
1036	                    if side is not None:
1037	                        relocate(blocker, side)
1038	                        relocate(robot, destination)
1039	                        robot.route.pop(0)
1040	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1041	                        continue
1042	                if blocker.route:
1043	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
1044	                    if (
1045	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
1046	                        and ahead not in occupied
1047	                        and ahead not in reserved
1048	                    ):
1049	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
1050	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
1051	                        blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
1052	                        continue
1053	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
1054	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
1055	            side = self._self_sidestep(
1056	                robot, task, occupied, reserved, frozenset(moved_ids)
1057	            )
1058	            if side is not None:
1059	                cell, route = side
1060	                relocate(robot, cell)
1061	                robot.route = route
1062	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1063	                continue
1064	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
1065	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
1066	        self.tick += 1
1067	        event: dict[str, object] = {
1068	            "type": "tick",
1069	            "tick": self.tick,
1070	            "moved": moved,
1071	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
1072	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
1073	        }
1074	        self.replay.append(event)
1075	        return event

1077	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:
1078	        if robot.task_id is None:
1079	            return
1080	        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
1081	        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1082	            return
1083	        if robot.position == task.pickup:
1084	            task.picked_up = True
1085	        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
1086	            task.completed = True
1087	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
1088	            robot.task_id = None

1130	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
1131	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
1132	
1133	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
1134	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
1135	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
1136	        raise :class:`OSError`.
1137	        """
1138	        document = {
1139	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
1140	            "grid": {
1141	                "width": self.grid.width,
1142	                "height": self.grid.height,
1143	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
1144	            },
1145	            "base_grid": {
1146	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
1147	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
1148	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
1149	            },
1150	            "tick": self.tick,
1151	            "robots": [
1152	                {
1153	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
1154	                    "position": list(robot.position),
1155	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
1156	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
1157	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
1158	                }
1159	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
1160	            ],
1161	            "tasks": [
1162	                {
1163	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
1164	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
1165	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
1166	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
1167	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
1168	                    "completed": task.completed,
1169	                }
1170	                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
1171	            ],
1172	            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
1173	            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
1174	            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
1175	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
1176	        }
1177	        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
1178	
1179	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
1180	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
1181	        try:
1182	            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
1183	            try:
1184	                handle.write(payload)
1185	                handle.flush()
1186	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
1187	            finally:
1188	                handle.close()
1189	            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
1190	            self._fsync_directory(directory)
1191	        except BaseException:
1192	            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
1193	            try:
1194	                os.unlink(tmp_name)
1195	            except OSError:
1196	                pass
1197	            raise

1213	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
1214	        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.
1215	
1216	        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
1217	        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
1218	        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
1219	        propagate as :class:`OSError`.
1220	        """
1221	        try:
1222	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
1223	                text = handle.read()
1224	        except OSError:
1225	            raise
1226	        try:
1227	            data = json.loads(text)

1232	    @classmethod
1233	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
1234	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
1235	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
1236	
1237	        version = data.get("version")
1238	        if not _is_int(version):
1239	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
1240	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
1241	            raise ValueError(
1242	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
1243	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
1244	            )
1245	
1246	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
1247	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
1248	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
1249	
1250	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1251	        paused: set[str] = set()
1252	        if version == 1:
1253	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
1254	            base_grid = grid
1255	        else:
1256	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
1257	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
1258	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
1259	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
1260	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
1261	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
1262	            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
1263	
1264	        robots: list[Robot] = []
1265	        for record in robot_records:
1266	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
1267	            if not grid.traversable(position):
1268	                raise ValueError(
1269	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
1270	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
1271	                )
1272	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
1273	            previous = position
1274	            for index, cell in enumerate(record["route"]):
1275	                waypoint = _as_pair(
1276	                    cell, f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {index}"
1277	                )
1278	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
1279	                    raise ValueError(
1280	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
1281	                        "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
1282	                    )
1283	                if abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0]) + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1]) != 1:
1284	                    raise ValueError(
1285	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
1286	                        f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
1287	                    )
1288	                route.append(waypoint)
1289	                previous = waypoint
1290	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
1291	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
1292	                raise ValueError(
1293	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
1294	                    "non-negative integer"
1295	                )
1296	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
1297	
1298	        tasks: list[Task] = []
1299	        for record in task_records:
1300	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
1301	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
1302	            tasks.append(
1303	                Task(
1304	                    record["task_id"],
1305	                    pickup,
1306	                    dropoff,
1307	                    record["assigned_robot"],
1308	                    record["picked_up"],
1309	                    record["completed"],
1310	                )
1311	            )
1312	
1313	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
1314	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
1315	
1316	        # Ownership is judged with the exact rules direct construction uses:
1317	        # mutual bindings for work in progress, historical owners for finished
1318	        # tasks, and a collected task that may never lack its carrier.
1319	        cls._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
1320	        for task in tasks:
1321	            if task.completed and not task.picked_up:
1322	                raise ValueError(
1323	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is completed but never picked up"
1324	                )
1325	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
1326	                # Direct construction never sees a finished task without a
1327	                # historical owner because it cannot create completion itself,
1328	                # but a checkpoint document can spell one, and the running
1329	                # simulator only ever saves picked-up tasks with a carrier.
1330	                raise ValueError(
1331	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
1332	                )
1333	
1334	        cls._validate_paused_state(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id, grid)
1335	        cls._validate_active_task_routes(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id)
1336	        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)
1337	
1338	        replay_change_frames = cls._replay_map_change_frames(replay)
1339	        if replay_change_frames != map_changes:
1340	            raise ValueError("replay map-change frames do not match 'map_changes' history")
1341	
1342	        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks)
1343	        simulator.base_grid = base_grid
1344	        simulator.tick = tick
1345	        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)
1346	        simulator.map_changes = copy.deepcopy(map_changes)
1347	        simulator._map_sequence = len(map_changes)
1348	        simulator.paused_tasks = set(paused)
1349	        simulator._traffic_waits = traffic_waits
1350	        # Version 1 has no edit history: its saved grid is the baseline and
1351	        # applies to every tick frame. Version 2 replays the recorded changes
1352	        # alongside the frames so each frame is judged against its contemporary
1353	        # map.
1354	        cls._validate_replay_positions(replay, tick, robot_by_id, base_grid, map_changes)
1355	        cls._validate_replay_completion(replay, tick, task_by_id)
